name: MuseTalk
license: creativeml-openrail-m (per HF Hub API license tag, checked 2026-09-10)
notes: Checked https://huggingface.co/api/models/TMElyralab/MuseTalk on 2026-09-10: repo-level license tag is 'creativeml-openrail-m' (the same family as SDXL's license above) -- permits commercial use but with use-based content restrictions baked into the license text itself. commercial_use_allowed left null pending reading the actual LICENSE file rather than trusting the tag alone; this is a stronger signal than 'unknown' but not a substitute for that read.

name: SadTalker
license: mit (per HF Hub API license tag, checked 2026-09-10)
notes: Checked https://huggingface.co/api/models/vinthony/SadTalker on 2026-09-10: repo-level license tag is 'mit'. commercial_use_allowed still left null because SadTalker's pipeline composes several third-party components (e.g. face-alignment, GFPGAN) each with their own license -- the top-level 'mit' tag doesn't cover those. Audit the full dependency chain, not just the top-level repo, before any use.

name: Wav2Lip
notes: The original repo's LICENSE explicitly restricts use to academic/research purposes and prohibits commercial use. No 07_GENERATION provider implements this: its checkpoint loading and face-detection preprocessing (S3FD) are involved enough that we chose not to write unverifiable integration code for it here. Free among the well-known open lip-sync options is largely a choice between 'no commercial license' (this) and 'license unclear' (MuseTalk/SadTalker above) -- there is no clearly commercial-friendly, well-established open-source lip-sync model at the time this registry was written. Re-check the landscape before committing to one.
